# Snippets the audit must classify. A checker that degraded into "return
# nothing" passes the real gate forever and reads as coverage, so it is made to
# prove it can still see — and to prove it can still tell a fenced argv from an
# unfenced one for EVERY binary in argfence's table, not just git.
#
# Each block is:
#   FLAG <name>   — the audit MUST report at least one finding
#   PASS <name>   — the audit MUST report none
# followed by one or more lines of Go, wrapped by the test into
#   func snippet(repoDir, branch, base, ref, path, msg, pkg, dir, fields, num,
#                file, lang, pattern, mutate, chosen string) { … }
#
# The floor is derived: TestAuditFlagsItsOwnSnippets asserts it exercised every
# row it parsed, so a row cannot be deleted or skipped without failing.

# --- git (Separator, --end-of-options for refs / -- for paths) ---

FLAG bare-var-positional
	gitCombined(repoDir, "branch", "-D", branch)

FLAG bare-var-after-subcommand
	gitNoOut(repoDir, "rev-parse", branch)

FLAG const-suffix-is-not-a-prefix
	gitTrim(repoDir, "ls-tree", ref+":.dross/phases")

FLAG exec-command-direct
	exec.Command("git", "-C", repoDir, "log", branch)

FLAG separator-after-the-value
	gitNoOut(repoDir, "rev-parse", branch, "--end-of-options")

FLAG path-without-separator
	gitCombined(repoDir, "add", path)

PASS all-literals
	gitCombined(repoDir, "fetch", "origin")

PASS const-prefix-concat
	gitNoOut(repoDir, "rev-parse", "--verify", "refs/heads/"+branch)

PASS ref-separator-then-value
	gitCombined(repoDir, "checkout", "--end-of-options", branch)

PASS path-separator-then-value
	gitNoOut(repoDir, "ls-files", "--error-unmatch", "--", path)

PASS option-argument-not-positional
	gitCombined(repoDir, "commit", "-m", msg)

PASS mixed-ref-and-path-separators
	gitCombined(repoDir, "checkout", "--end-of-options", ref, "--", path)

# --- gh (Separator, --; cobra ENDS flag parsing there) ---
#
# gh was out of scope while the gate was git-only, and was passing config-derived
# values the whole time. It is in scope now, which is what this row records.

FLAG gh-bare-positional
	ghCommand("pr", "view", num)

FLAG gh-exec-direct-bare-positional
	exec.Command("gh", "pr", "view", num)

PASS gh-flags-before-separator
	ghCommand("pr", "view", "--json", fields, "--", num)

# A `--` in cobra ends flag parsing entirely rather than fencing one token, so a
# flag AFTER it becomes a positional. `gh pr view` takes at most one and exits
# "accepts at most 1 arg(s), received 3"; `gh pr comment` posts the wrong body.
# Both are green against a ghCommand test double, which is how this shape got
# written in the first place.
FLAG gh-flag-demoted-past-separator
	ghCommand("pr", "view", "--", num, "--json", fields)

PASS gh-value-slot-needs-no-separator
	ghCommand("pr", "list", "--base", base, "--state", "open")

# --- ast-grep (Separator, --) ---

FLAG ast-grep-bare-file
	exec.Command("ast-grep", "run", "--lang", lang, "--pattern", pattern, file)

PASS ast-grep-separator-before-operand
	exec.Command("ast-grep", "run", "--lang", lang, "--pattern", pattern, "--json=compact", "--", file)

# --- gremlins / npx / dotnet (Reject — no end-of-options token exists) ---

FLAG gremlins-bare-pkg
	exec.Command("gremlins", "unleash", pkg)

# The distinguishing row for the Reject policy: a separator does NOT rescue a
# tool that has none. gremlins would read "--" as a package path.
FLAG gremlins-separator-does-not-rescue
	exec.Command("gremlins", "unleash", "--", pkg)

PASS gremlins-const-prefixed-pkg
	exec.Command("gremlins", "unleash", "./"+pkg)

PASS gremlins-option-argument
	exec.Command("gremlins", "unleash", "--output", path, "./"+pkg)

FLAG dotnet-bare-positional
	exec.Command("dotnet", "stryker", dir)

PASS dotnet-option-argument
	exec.Command("dotnet", "stryker", "--output", dir)

FLAG npx-bare-positional
	exec.Command("npx", "--yes", "@stryker-mutator/core@9.6.1", "run", mutate)

PASS npx-option-argument
	exec.Command("npx", "--yes", "@stryker-mutator/core@9.6.1", "run", "--mutate", mutate, "--reporters", "json")

# --- fail-closed ---

FLAG unknown-binary-has-no-policy
	exec.Command("cargo", "test", pkg)

FLAG non-literal-binary-unresolvable
	exec.Command(chosen, "install")
